correctness.rationale: For every full-dimensional tetrahedron, triangular shadow directions are exactly the disjoint four pairs of spherical vertex tangent cones. On each cone the projected area equals the area of the opposite face times its normal coordinate. Spherical integration by parts with Laplacians -2 and -6 for linear and traceless quadratic coordinate functions yields exact cone moment sums; the outward conormal and great-circle arc integrals are explicit. Cauchy brightness plus the exact correlated-Gaussian absolute-value kernel proves the unconditional moments, so the quadrilateral conditional moments follow by subtraction. For the regular tetrahedron, face areas, dot products, solid angles, and cone moments yield all four closed expressions and the strict selection bias. Independent deterministic cone quadrature and random convex-hull diagnostics match the proof formulas; they are not substituted for proof.
risks: Numerical cone quadrature does not prove the all-tetrahedra claim; the analytical Green identities do.
The outward face-normal and spherical conormal orientation must be kept fixed and is explicitly specified.

originality.rationale: Feldman--Klain prove the unweighted vertex-angle probability but not the first/second area-weighted cone masses. Finch evaluates unconditional regular-tetrahedron projected-area moments and the separate 3/4 vertex probabilities and presents a piecewise directional area integrand, but does not state the conditional first or second moment table or a finite angle formula for arbitrary asymmetric tetrahedra. Black--Criado focus on shadow size, edge lengths, and normal fans. Combining the older results does not by itself provide the independent weighted cone integrations and the arbitrary-shape formulas. Searches across mathematical aliases located no domination; historical unindexed coverage remains possible.
residual_risks: An older or unindexed stereology or projection-shadow paper might contain an equivalent weighted cone-moment identity.

value.rationale: Tetrahedral shadows are the first polyhedral family where random planar silhouettes have two possible vertex counts. Existing primary sources compute their frequencies and unconditional projected areas separately. In stereology and imaging, conditioning on a visible silhouette class changes the sampling distribution of areas. The new arbitrary-tetrahedron finite angle formulas are shape-sensitive yet require no probabilistic integration; they quantify first and second conditional area moments, and the regular example demonstrates a provable nonzero selection bias plus markedly different conditional variances. This is a motivated all-object invariant rather than a parameter-substitution exercise.
risks: Results are specific to uniform orthogonal projections in three dimensions; analogous other shadow statistics remain open.
